--- /dev/null
+++ /home/agent/workspace/semantics.txt
@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+Semantics: abs — Small-Step Operational Semantics
+
+1. Abstract Syntax
+    Expressions  e ::= n            integer literals, n in Z
+                 |  abs(e)          absolute value application
+                 |  e1 + e2         integer addition
+
+    Values       v ::= n            (a subset of expressions)
+
+2. Evaluation Relation
+    The small-step evaluation relation  ->  is the smallest binary
+    relation on expressions such that every instance of the inference
+    rules below holds.
+
+        Notation:   e -> e'      "e steps to e' in one step"
+                    e ->* e'     reflexive-transitive closure of ->
+
+3. Inference Rules
+
+    --- Congruence (evaluation contexts) ---
+
+    (S-ABS)                 e  ->  e'
+                        -----------------
+                        abs(e) -> abs(e')
+
+    (S-ADD-L)     e1 -> e1'
+                -----------------
+                e1 + e2 -> e1' + e2
+
+    (S-ADD-R)     e2 -> e2'
+                -----------------
+                n + e2 -> n + e2'
+
+    --- Reduction (computation) rules ---
+
+    (R-ADD)    n1 + n2 -> n3        where n3 = n1 + n2   (integer sum)
+
+    (R-ABS-POS)   abs(n) -> n       if n >= 0
+
+    (R-ABS-NEG)   abs(n) -> n'      if n < 0  and  n' = -n
+
+4. Derived Properties
+
+    P1 (Progress)     If e is a closed, well-formed expression, then
+                      either e is a value or there exists e' with
+                      e -> e'.
+
+    P2 (Determinism)  If e -> e1 and e -> e2, then e1 = e2.
+                      (The side conditions on R-ABS-POS and
+                      R-ABS-NEG are exclusive and exhaustive.)
+
+    P3 (Termination)  Every closed expression e reduces to a value:
+                      there exists n with e ->* n. Each step strictly
+                      decreases expression size; rules never enlarge
+                      terms.
+
+5. Correspondence with the Specification (spec.txt)
+
+    The reduction rules R-ABS-POS and R-ABS-NEG realize exactly the
+    defining clauses of abs:
+
+        R-ABS-POS  realizes  abs(x) =  x   if x >= 0
+        R-ABS-NEG  realizes  abs(x) = -x   if x <  0
+
+    Consequently, for every closed expression e that reduces to n:
+
+        abs(n) ->* m   with  m >= 0  and  m = n if n >= 0, m = -n otherwise
+
+    i.e. m satisfies properties P1-P3 of spec.txt.
+
+6. Example Derivation
+
+    abs(-3 + 1)
+      -> abs(-2)          by S-ABS with R-ADD on the subterm (-3 + 1 -> -2)
+      -> 2                by R-ABS-NEG
+      ->* 2               (value reached)
